local http = require("http")
local json = require("json")
local funcs = require("funcs")
local security = require("security")

local function handler()
    local res = http.response()
    local req = http.request()
    if not res or not req then return nil, "no http context" end
    res:set_content_type(http.CONTENT.JSON)
    -- Endpoints attach to a router that enforces auth; this guards the rare
    -- unauthenticated path defensively.
    local actor = security.actor()
    if not actor then
        res:set_status(http.STATUS.UNAUTHORIZED)
        res:write_json({ success = false, error = "authentication required" })
        return
    end

    local raw, raw_err = req:body()
    if raw_err or type(raw) ~= "string" then
        res:set_status(http.STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)
        res:write_json({ success = false, error = "invalid request body" })
        return
    end
    local body, body_err = json.decode(raw)
    if body_err or type(body) ~= "table" then
        res:set_status(http.STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)
        res:write_json({ success = false, error = "invalid json" })
        return
    end

    local result, err = funcs.call("kickside.skills:skill_create", {
        name = body.name,
        description = body.description,
        body = body.body,
        status = body.status,
        agent_id = body.agent_id,
        icon = body.icon,
    })
    if err then
        res:set_status(http.STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)
        res:write_json({ success = false, error = tostring(err) })
        return
    end
    res:set_status(http.STATUS.OK)
    res:write_json({ success = true, skill_id = result })
end

return { handler = handler }

local http = require("http")

local M = {}

type IntOptions = {
    min: integer?,
    max: integer?,
}

local function bounds_error(name: string, opts: IntOptions?): string
    local min_value = opts and opts.min or nil
    local max_value = opts and opts.max or nil
    if min_value ~= nil and max_value ~= nil then
        return name .. " must be between " .. tostring(min_value) .. " and " .. tostring(max_value)
    end
    if min_value ~= nil then return name .. " must be >= " .. tostring(min_value) end
    if max_value ~= nil then return name .. " must be <= " .. tostring(max_value) end
    return name .. " is out of range"
end

function M.query_int(req: any, key: string, default_value: integer?, opts: IntOptions?): (integer?, string?)
    local raw = req:query(key)
    if raw == nil or raw == "" then return default_value, nil end
    if type(raw) ~= "string" then return nil, key .. " must be an integer" end

    local value = tonumber(raw)
    if not value or value ~= math.floor(value) then
        return nil, key .. " must be an integer"
    end

    local int_value = value :: integer
    if opts and opts.min ~= nil and int_value < opts.min then return nil, bounds_error(key, opts) end
    if opts and opts.max ~= nil and int_value > opts.max then return nil, bounds_error(key, opts) end
    return int_value, nil
end

function M.bad_request(res: any, message: string): ()
    res:set_status(http.STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)
    res:write_json({ success = false, error = message })
end

return M

-- SKILL.md frontmatter parser — a bounded reader for the open SKILL.md format
-- (agentskills.io), NOT a general YAML parser. It handles exactly what the format
-- uses: a leading `---`-delimited block of `key: value` pairs, an optional nested
-- `metadata:` map (one level of two-space indentation), and list values written
-- either inline (`[a, b]`) or as `-` items. `allowed-tools` is split on spaces
-- when given as a bare scalar (the Claude convention). Anything richer is out of
-- scope by design; a focused parser is correct here and avoids a YAML dependency
-- the module lacks.

local M = {}

type Frontmatter = { [string]: any }

-- Trim ASCII whitespace from both ends of a string.
local function trim(s: string): string
    return (s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""))
end
M.trim = trim

-- Strip a single pair of matching surrounding quotes from a scalar value.
local function unquote(s: string): string
    local first = s:sub(1, 1)
    if (first == '"' or first == "'") and s:sub(-1) == first and #s >= 2 then
        return s:sub(2, #s - 1)
    end
    return s
end

-- Count leading spaces (indentation depth) of a raw line.
local function indent_of(line: string): integer
    local sp = line:match("^( *)")
    return (sp and #sp or 0) :: integer
end

-- Parse an inline list `[a, b, c]` into a string array; returns nil if not inline.
local function parse_inline_list(v: string): { string }?
    if v:sub(1, 1) ~= "[" or v:sub(-1) ~= "]" then return nil end
    local inner = v:sub(2, #v - 1)
    local out: { string } = {}
    for item in inner:gmatch("[^,]+") do
        local t = unquote(trim(item))
        if t ~= "" then out[#out + 1] = t end
    end
    return out
end

-- Split the frontmatter block into its lines (without the fences) and the body.
-- Returns (lines, body) or (nil, full_text) when there is no frontmatter block.
local function split_block(text: string): ({ string }?, string)
    -- Tolerate a UTF-8 BOM and leading blank lines before the opening fence.
    local s = text:gsub("^\239\187\191", "")
    local rest = s:match("^%s*%-%-%-[ \t]*\r?\n(.*)$")
    if not rest then return nil, s end

    local lines: { string } = {}
    local body_start: number? = nil
    local pos = 1
    while true do
        local nl = rest:find("\n", pos, true)
        local line = nl and rest:sub(pos, nl - 1) or rest:sub(pos)
        local stripped = line:gsub("\r$", "")
        if stripped:match("^%-%-%-[ \t]*$") then
            body_start = nl and (nl + 1) or (#rest + 1)
            break
        end
        lines[#lines + 1] = stripped
        if not nl then break end
        pos = nl + 1
    end
    local body = body_start and rest:sub(body_start) or ""
    return lines, body
end

-- Parse a SKILL.md document. Returns (frontmatter, body). frontmatter is a map of
-- lowercased keys to values: scalars are strings, lists are string arrays, and a
-- nested `metadata:` block becomes a sub-map. When there is no frontmatter block
-- the whole text is the body and frontmatter is {}.
function M.parse(text: any): (Frontmatter, string)
    if type(text) ~= "string" then return {}, "" end
    local lines, body = split_block(text :: string)
    if not lines then return {}, body end

    local fm: Frontmatter = {}
    local i = 1
    local n = #lines
    while i <= n do
        local line = lines[i]
        local stripped = trim(line)
        -- Skip blanks, comments, and stray top-level list items.
        if stripped ~= "" and stripped:sub(1, 1) ~= "#" and indent_of(line) == 0 then
            local key, val = line:match("^([%w_%-]+)%s*:%s*(.*)$")
            if key and val then
                local lkey = key:lower()
                val = trim(val)

                if val == "" then
                    -- A bare `key:` introduces either a nested map (indented
                    -- `subkey: value`) or a list (indented `- item`). Peek ahead.
                    local sub: Frontmatter = {}
                    local list: { string } = {}
                    local j = i + 1
                    while j <= n do
                        local nxt = lines[j]
                        if trim(nxt) == "" then j = j + 1
                        elseif indent_of(nxt) > 0 then
                            local item = trim(nxt):match("^%-%s*(.*)$")
                            if item then
                                list[#list + 1] = unquote(trim(item))
                            else
                                local sk, sv = trim(nxt):match("^([%w_%-]+)%s*:%s*(.*)$")
                                if sk then sub[sk:lower()] = unquote(trim(sv)) end
                            end
                            j = j + 1
                        else
                            break
                        end
                    end
                    i = j - 1
                    if #list > 0 then
                        fm[lkey] = list
                    elseif next(sub) ~= nil then
                        fm[lkey] = sub
                    else
                        fm[lkey] = ""
                    end
                else
                    local inline = parse_inline_list(val)
                    if inline then
                        fm[lkey] = inline
                    elseif lkey == "allowed-tools" or lkey == "allowed_tools" then
                        -- Claude convention: a bare scalar lists tools space-split.
                        local tools: { string } = {}
                        for t in (unquote(val)):gmatch("%S+") do tools[#tools + 1] = t end
                        fm[lkey] = tools
                    else
                        fm[lkey] = unquote(val)
                    end
                end
            end
        end
        i = i + 1
    end

    return fm, body
end

return M

-- Bundle normalization — turn parsed frontmatter + body + a flat list of fetched
-- files into the canonical SkillBundle the store consumes. Pure logic; no IO. A
-- source's fetch() builds the raw file list (path + content + encoding); this maps
-- frontmatter scalars to the bundle's typed fields and classifies each file
-- (reference / asset / script) by its path, inferring a mime type and, for
-- scripts, the language from the extension.

local skill_types = require("types")

local M = {}

-- Non-empty string guard shared across the store sides.
function M.is_str(v: any): boolean
    return type(v) == "string" and (v :: string) ~= ""
end

-- Normalize a bundle-relative path: forbid absolute paths and `..` traversal,
-- collapse leading slashes, reject the empty string. Returns (clean, nil) or
-- (nil, err). Centralized here so the writer (file prep) and reader (read_file)
-- enforce one path policy.
function M.clean_path(path: any): (string?, string?)
    if not M.is_str(path) then return nil, "path is required" end
    local p = (path :: string):gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("^/+", "")
    if p == "" then return nil, "path is required" end
    if #p > skill_types.LIMITS.PATH then return nil, "path too long" end
    for seg in p:gmatch("[^/]+") do
        if seg == ".." then return nil, "path traversal is not allowed" end
    end
    return p
end

-- Map a file extension to a mime type. Covers the text/markdown/code formats a
-- skill bundle carries; unknown extensions fall back to a generic binary type.
local MIME = {
    md = "text/markdown",
    markdown = "text/markdown",
    txt = "text/plain",
    json = "application/json",
    yaml = "application/yaml",
    yml = "application/yaml",
    csv = "text/csv",
    html = "text/html",
    py = "text/x-python",
    js = "text/javascript",
    ts = "text/typescript",
    sh = "text/x-shellscript",
    lua = "text/x-lua",
    rb = "text/x-ruby",
    png = "image/png",
    jpg = "image/jpeg",
    jpeg = "image/jpeg",
    gif = "image/gif",
    pdf = "application/pdf",
}

-- Map a script file extension to a language label stored in the file metadata.
-- The future script runner reads this to pick a runtime profile.
local SCRIPT_LANG = {
    py = "python",
    js = "javascript",
    ts = "typescript",
    sh = "bash",
    lua = "lua",
    rb = "ruby",
}

local function ext_of(path: string): string
    return (path:match("%.([%w]+)$") or ""):lower()
end

M.ext_of = ext_of

-- Classify a file by its repo-relative path. scripts/ → script, assets/ →
-- asset, everything else (references/, loose files) → reference.
function M.kind_for_path(path: string): string
    local p = path:lower()
    if p:match("^scripts/") or p:match("/scripts/") then return skill_types.FILE_KIND.SCRIPT end
    if p:match("^assets/") or p:match("/assets/") then return skill_types.FILE_KIND.ASSET end
    return skill_types.FILE_KIND.REFERENCE
end

function M.mime_for_path(path: string): string
    return MIME[ext_of(path)] or "application/octet-stream"
end

-- Normalize a single fetched file (kind/mime/metadata derived from the path; an
-- explicit kind on the input wins so a source can override). The returned table
-- carries content + encoding for the store to decode, so it is the raw fetched
-- shape rather than the stored SkillFile type.
function M.normalize_file(raw: any): skill_types.SkillFileInput
    local file = (type(raw) == "table" and raw or {}) :: skill_types.SkillFileInput
    local path = type(file.path) == "string" and file.path or ""
    local kind = type(file.kind) == "string" and (file.kind :: string) ~= "" and file.kind or M.kind_for_path(path)
    local mime = type(file.mime_type) == "string" and (file.mime_type :: string) ~= "" and file.mime_type or M.mime_for_path(path)

    local metadata: skill_types.Map = type(file.metadata) == "table" and (file.metadata :: skill_types.Map) or {}
    if kind == skill_types.FILE_KIND.SCRIPT then
        local lang = SCRIPT_LANG[ext_of(path)]
        if lang and metadata.language == nil then metadata.language = lang end
    end

    return {
        path = path,
        kind = kind,
        mime_type = mime,
        content = file.content,
        encoding = file.encoding,
        executable = kind == skill_types.FILE_KIND.SCRIPT and true or (file.executable == true),
        metadata = metadata,
    }
end

-- Coerce a frontmatter value (scalar/list) to a string array.
local function to_list(v: any): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    if type(v) == "table" then
        for _, item in ipairs(v :: { any }) do
            if type(item) == "string" and (item :: string) ~= "" then out[#out + 1] = item :: string end
        end
    elseif type(v) == "string" and (v :: string) ~= "" then
        for t in (v :: string):gmatch("%S+") do out[#out + 1] = t end
    end
    return out
end

M.to_list = to_list

-- Build a SkillBundle from parsed frontmatter, the markdown body, the raw file
-- list, and the source descriptor. The name falls back to the supplied default
-- (e.g. a directory name) when frontmatter omits it.
function M.to_bundle(fm: any, body: any, files: any, source: any, name_fallback: string?): skill_types.SkillBundle
    local frontmatter = (type(fm) == "table" and fm or {}) :: skill_types.Map
    local name = type(frontmatter.name) == "string" and (frontmatter.name :: string) ~= "" and frontmatter.name or (name_fallback or "")

    local norm_files: { skill_types.SkillFileInput } = {}
    if type(files) == "table" then
        for _, f in ipairs(files :: { skill_types.SkillFileInput }) do
            norm_files[#norm_files + 1] = M.normalize_file(f)
        end
    end

    return ({
        name = name,
        description = type(frontmatter.description) == "string" and frontmatter.description or "",
        version = type(frontmatter.version) == "string" and frontmatter.version or nil,
        body = type(body) == "string" and body or "",
        license = type(frontmatter.license) == "string" and frontmatter.license or nil,
        allowed_tools = to_list(frontmatter["allowed-tools"] or frontmatter.allowed_tools),
        compatibility = type(frontmatter.compatibility) == "table" and (frontmatter.compatibility :: skill_types.Map) or {},
        metadata = type(frontmatter.metadata) == "table" and (frontmatter.metadata :: skill_types.Map) or {},
        files = norm_files,
        source = type(source) == "table" and (source :: skill_types.Map) or {},
    }) :: skill_types.SkillBundle
end

return M

-- Skill's kickside.contract:deletable adapter. By canon a skill's history IS its
-- component's primary thread (thread_id == skill_id), reaped by the component-driven
-- delete cascade (teardown purges the primary thread). So the only separate data this
-- deletable owns is the bundle upload (file artifacts + blobs). delete_component on a
-- skill -- including the transfer orchestrator's batch rollback -- cascades cleanly.

local ctx = require("ctx")
local upload_lib = require("upload_lib")

local function handle(request_dto)
    local component_id, err = ctx.get("component_id")
    if err or not component_id then
        return { success = false, error = "no component context" }
    end
    local skill_id = tostring(component_id)

    -- Bundle upload: artifacts + blobs + the upload row (upload_id = skill_id).
    upload_lib.delete_upload(skill_id)

    return { success = true }
end

return { handle = handle }

-- Skill's kickside.contract:portable EXPORT adapter. A skill's data is its version
-- history (the projection body folded from its thread events) and its file bytes
-- (upload artifacts). This streams the version records to <path>/data/versions.jsonl
-- and each referenced artifact's RAW bytes to its own part file under
-- <path>/data/artifacts/<artifact_id>, with a small metadata index in
-- data/artifacts.jsonl. The component shell (title/description/status meta) is written
-- by the generic coordinator; this moves only the skill's own data.
--
-- Bytes travel raw (the KXB1 container carries length-delimited parts), never base64
-- in a single buffer: peak memory is one artifact, not every artifact at once -- a
-- skill with many or large file artifacts exports without buffering them all.

local fs = require("fs")
local ctx = require("ctx")
local state = require("skill_state")
local artifact_content_repo = require("artifact_content_repo")
local pio = require("portable_io")

local M = {}

function M.handler(args)
    local component_id = ctx.get("component_id")
    if type(component_id) ~= "string" or component_id == "" then
        return { success = false, error = "no component_id in context" }
    end
    local storage_id = type(args) == "table" and args.storage_id or nil
    local path = type(args) == "table" and args.path or nil
    if type(storage_id) ~= "string" or type(path) ~= "string" then
        return { success = false, error = "storage_id and path are required" }
    end

    local storage, ferr = fs.get(storage_id)
    if not storage then return { success = false, error = "storage: " .. tostring(ferr) } end

    local body, berr = state.body_for(component_id)

    local base = path .. "/data/"

    -- the index. read_artifact_content returns one artifact's bytes, so the working set
    -- never exceeds the largest single artifact.
    local seen = {}
    local index = {}
    for _, v in ipairs(versions) do
        for _, f in ipairs(type(v.files) == "table" and v.files or {}) do
            local aid = tostring(f.artifact_id or "")
            if aid ~= "" and not seen[aid] then
                seen[aid] = true
                local content, rerr = artifact_content_repo.read_artifact_content(component_id, aid)
                if rerr or content == nil then
                    return { success = false, error = "read artifact " .. aid .. ": " .. tostring(rerr) }
                end
                if type(content) ~= "string" then
                    return { success = false, error = "read artifact " .. aid .. ": expected string content" }
                end

                local apath = path .. "/" .. rel
                pio.ensure_parent(storage, apath)
                local wok, werr = storage:writefile(apath, content)
                if not wok then return { success = false, error = "write artifact " .. aid .. ": " .. tostring(werr) } end
                index[#index + 1] = {
                    artifact_id = aid, mime_type = f.mime_type, kind = f.kind, path = f.path,
                }
                files[#files + 1] = rel
            end
        end
    end

    local ok1, werr1 = pio.write_jsonl(storage, base .. "versions.jsonl", versions)
    if not ok1 then return { success = false, error = "write versions: " .. tostring(werr1) } end
    local ok2, werr2 = pio.write_jsonl(storage, base .. "artifacts.jsonl", index)
    if not ok2 then return { success = false, error = "write artifacts index: " .. tostring(werr2) } end

    return {
        success = true,
        manifest = {
            files = files,
            counts = { versions = #versions, artifacts = #index },
        },
    }
end

return M

-- Skill's kickside.contract:portable IMPORT_INTO adapter. The coordinator has
-- already registered the new skill component (component_id is in context); this
-- replays <path>/data/*.jsonl into it: it ensures the skill's history thread +
-- projection + bundle upload, re-stores each exported artifact's bytes under the
-- new skill (recording old artifact_id -> new), and appends one version event per
-- exported version (created for v1, updated after) with its file manifest remapped
-- to the new artifact ids. The events drive the projection that rebuilds the body.

local fs = require("fs")
local ctx = require("ctx")
local security = require("security")
local contract = require("contract")
local errors = require("errors")
local types = require("types")
local state = require("skill_state")
local artifact_content_repo = require("artifact_content_repo")
local upload_record_repo = require("upload_record_repo")
local skill_storage = require("skill_storage")
local pio = require("portable_io")

local M = {}

local function actor_id(): string
    local actor = security.actor()
    if not actor then return "" end
    local id = actor:id()
    return id and tostring(id) or ""
end

-- The one canonical threads seam: the kickside.core:threads contract, opened under
-- the caller's actor + scope, never a private *_method function-id.
local THREADS_CONTRACT = "kickside.core:threads"

local function threads(): (any?, string?)
    local def, gerr = contract.get(THREADS_CONTRACT)
    if gerr or not def then return nil, "threads contract unavailable: " .. tostring(gerr) end
    local inst, oerr = (def :: any):with_actor(security.actor()):with_scope(security.scope()):open()
    if oerr or not inst then return nil, "threads open failed: " .. tostring(oerr) end
    return inst, nil
end

function M.handler(args)
    local component_id = ctx.get("component_id")
    if type(component_id) ~= "string" or component_id == "" then
        return { success = false, error = "no component_id in context" }
    end
    local skill_id = component_id :: string
    local storage_id = type(args) == "table" and args.storage_id or nil
    local path = type(args) == "table" and args.path or nil
    if type(storage_id) ~= "string" or type(path) ~= "string" then
        return { success = false, error = "storage_id and path are required" }
    end

    local storage, ferr = fs.get(storage_id)
    if not storage then return { success = false, error = "storage: " .. tostring(ferr) } end

    local base = path .. "/data/"
    local versions = pio.read_jsonl(storage, base .. "versions.jsonl") or {}
    -- artifacts.jsonl is a metadata index; each artifact's bytes live in its own
    -- part file under data/artifacts/<artifact_id>, read back one at a time.
    local artifacts = pio.read_jsonl(storage, base .. "artifacts.jsonl") or {}
    if #versions == 0 then return { success = false, error = "missing versions.jsonl" } end

    -- The history thread passes the skill kind as its declaration impl_id, so the
    -- engine auto-applies its declared projection on creation. The thread component
    -- shell itself remains kickside.core:thread -- no register here.
    local thread_id, terr = state.thread_for(skill_id)
    if terr or not thread_id then return { success = false, error = "thread: " .. tostring(terr) } end

    -- Bundle upload for the new skill's artifacts.
    local _, uerr = upload_record_repo.create(
        skill_id, actor_id(), 1, "application/x-skill-bundle",
        skill_storage.id(), "skill-bundle/" .. skill_id, "skill_bundle", { skill_id = skill_id }, "completed"
    )
    if uerr and not errors.is(uerr, errors.CONFLICT) then
        return { success = false, error = "bundle upload: " .. tostring(uerr) }
    end

    -- Re-store each exported artifact under the new skill from its part file (one at a
    -- time, so memory never exceeds the largest single artifact); map old id -> new id.
    local amap = {}
    for _, a in ipairs(artifacts) do
        local aid = tostring(a.artifact_id or "")
        local bytes = storage:readfile(base .. "artifacts/" .. aid)
        if type(bytes) ~= "string" then
            return { success = false, error = "missing artifact bytes for " .. aid }
        end
        local artifact, aerr = artifact_content_repo.create_artifact({
            upload_id = skill_id,
            kind = tostring(a.kind or "asset"),
            mime_type = a.mime_type or "application/octet-stream",
            content = bytes,
            label = a.path,
        })
        if aerr or not artifact then return { success = false, error = "store artifact: " .. tostring(aerr) } end
        amap[aid] = tostring((artifact :: any).artifact_id)
    end

    -- Replay versions in order, remapping each file's artifact_id.
    table.sort(versions, function(x, y) return (tonumber(x.version) or 0) < (tonumber(y.version) or 0) end)
    for i, v in ipairs(versions) do
        local files = {}
        for _, f in ipairs(type(v.files) == "table" and v.files or {}) do
            local nf = {}
            for k, val in pairs(f) do nf[k] = val end
            nf.artifact_id = amap[tostring(f.artifact_id or "")] or f.artifact_id
            files[#files + 1] = nf
        end
        local record = {
            skill_id = skill_id,
            version = tonumber(v.version) or i,
            body = tostring(v.body or ""),
            name = v.name, description = v.description, license = v.license,
            allowed_tools = v.allowed_tools, compatibility = v.compatibility,
            metadata = v.metadata, source = v.source,
            files = files, file_count = #files, bundle_size = tonumber(v.bundle_size) or 0,
        }
        local etype = i == 1 and types.EVENT.CREATED or types.EVENT.UPDATED
        local inst, terr = threads()
        if terr then return { success = false, error = "append version: " .. terr } end
        local _, aerr = inst:emit({
            component_id = thread_id,
            type = etype, role = "user", body = record,
            impl_id = types.SKILL_IMPL,
            thread_class = types.THREAD_CLASS,
            content = { content_type = "text/markdown", content_mode = "inline", content_bytes = #record.body },
        })
        if aerr then return { success = false, error = "append version: " .. tostring(aerr) } end
    end

    return { success = true, id_map = { artifacts = amap }, warnings = {} }
end

return M

-- Skill-id set helpers shared by the three skills-trait surfaces: init_skills
-- (pins compile-time ids), skill_tool (activate/deactivate), and active_skills
-- (injects the active bodies). One place owns "normalize a context value into a
-- clean id list" plus the add/remove/has set ops, so the callers stay in sync.

local M = {}

-- Normalize a context value into a de-duplicated list of non-empty string ids,
-- in first-seen order. Accepts an array (trait_contexts / session context) or a
-- comma/space separated string (tolerant of a flat form field); else empty.
function M.parse(v: any): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
    local function push(id: string)
        if id ~= "" and not seen[id] then
            seen[id] = true
            out[#out + 1] = id
        end
    end
    if type(v) == "table" then
        for _, id in ipairs(v :: { any }) do
            if type(id) == "string" then push(id :: string) end
        end
    elseif type(v) == "string" then
        for id in string.gmatch(v :: string, "[^,%s]+") do push(id) end
    end
    return out
end

function M.has(list: { string }, id: string): boolean
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do
        if v == id then return true end
    end
    return false
end

-- Return a new list with id appended if absent; never mutates the input.
function M.add(list: { string }, id: string): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do out[#out + 1] = v end
    if id ~= "" and not M.has(out, id) then out[#out + 1] = id end
    return out
end

-- Return a new list with every occurrence of id removed.
function M.remove(list: { string }, id: string): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do
        if v ~= id then out[#out + 1] = v end
    end
    return out
end

return M

-- Skills trait prompt func — folds the session's ACTIVE skills into the prompt
-- on every step. The agent activates a skill with the Skill tool, which writes
-- the id into the session context (active_skills) via a control directive; this
-- reads that set back each step and injects the bodies, so an activated skill
-- stays in the prompt until the agent deactivates it.
--
-- Distinct from init_skills: that pins the compile-time skills the user chose on
-- the agent; this is the agent's own runtime set, curated mid-session and
-- persisted in the session context (so it survives a process restart).

local funcs = require("funcs")
local ctx = require("ctx")
local active_set = require("active_set")
local skill_types = require("types")

local SKILL_GET = "kickside.skills:skill_get"

-- The agent runtime calls a prompt func with no args and reads runtime state via
-- ctx. We return the active-skills section (or "" when none are active); the
-- runtime appends a non-empty return to the system prompt for this step.
local function execute(): string
    local raw = ctx.get("active_skills")
    local ids = active_set.parse(raw)
    if #ids == 0 then return "" end

    local sections: { string } = {}
    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
        -- Runs under the step's actor; a skill the actor can no longer read is
        -- skipped rather than failing the step.
        local skill, err = funcs.call(SKILL_GET, { skill_id = id })
        if not err and type(skill) == "table" then
            local s = skill :: skill_types.Skill
            if s.body ~= "" then
            sections[#sections + 1] = "### " .. tostring(s.name or "Skill") .. "\n" .. tostring(s.body)
            end
        end
    end
    if #sections == 0 then return "" end

    return "## Active skills\n\n" ..
        "You activated these; follow them directly. Deactivate one with the " ..
        "Skill tool's `deactivate` action when you no longer need it.\n\n" ..
        table.concat(sections, "\n\n")
end

return { execute = execute }

-- Skills trait build function — pins specific skills into an agent at compile time.
--
-- The skills trait is dynamic: its static prompt + Skill tool let an agent
-- discover, load, and activate ANY readable skill on demand. When an agent also
-- supplies `skill_ids` in the trait context, this build func loads those skills'
-- bodies and folds them straight into the system prompt, so one or two skills are
-- "baked in" without a tool round-trip. It runs under the agent loader's actor
-- (chat = the user; dataflow = the run's actor) via the compiler's funcs executor,
-- so a skill the actor cannot read is skipped rather than failing the compile.

local funcs = require("funcs")
local active_set = require("active_set")
local skill_types = require("types")

local SKILL_GET = "kickside.skills:skill_get"
local SKILL_LIST_FILES = "kickside.skills:skill_list_files"

-- The compiler invokes a build func as build(base_prompt, merged_context). The
-- compiler already appends the trait's static prompt separately, so we return
-- ONLY the pinned-skills section (or an empty contribution when nothing is pinned).
local function execute(base_prompt: any, context: any): skill_types.Contribution
    local trait_context = (type(context) == "table" and context or {}) :: skill_types.Map
    local ids = active_set.parse(trait_context.skill_ids)
    if #ids == 0 then return {} end

    local sections: { string } = {}
    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
        local skill, err = funcs.call(SKILL_GET, { skill_id = id })
        if not err and type(skill) == "table" then
            local s = skill :: skill_types.Skill
            if s.body ~= "" then
            local section = "### " .. tostring(s.name or "Skill") .. "\n" .. tostring(s.body)
            -- Inject only the file MANIFEST (paths + kind), never the file
            -- contents — the agent reads a file on demand via the SkillFile tool.
            local files = funcs.call(SKILL_LIST_FILES, { skill_id = id })
            local manifest = (type(files) == "table" and files or {}) :: { skill_types.SkillFile }
            if #manifest > 0 then
                local fl: { string } = { "\n\n**Files** (read with the SkillFile tool):" }
                for _, f in ipairs(manifest) do
                    fl[#fl + 1] = "- `" .. tostring(f.path) .. "` (" .. tostring(f.kind) .. ")"
                end
                section = section .. table.concat(fl, "\n")
            end
            sections[#sections + 1] = section
            end
        end
    end

    if #sections == 0 then return {} end

    local header = "## Pinned skills\n\n" ..
        "These skills are loaded and ready. Follow them directly when relevant; " ..
        "use the Skill tool to discover, load, or refine others.\n\n"
    return { prompt = header .. table.concat(sections, "\n\n") }
end

return { execute = execute }

-- SkillFile tool — read a skill bundle's files on demand.
--
-- A skill's `use` action returns the body plus a compact file manifest (paths +
-- kind, not contents). When the agent needs a referenced file it calls this tool:
-- `list` re-lists the manifest, `read` pulls one file's contents. Both go through
-- the access-checked skill_runtime contract (READ access + path normalization +
-- size cap enforced in the store). Binary assets come back base64-encoded.

local funcs = require("funcs")
local skill_types = require("types")

local SKILL_LIST_FILES = "kickside.skills:skill_list_files"
local SKILL_READ_FILE = "kickside.skills:skill_read_file"

local function tool_args(args: any): skill_types.SkillToolArgs
    if type(args) == "table" then return (args :: any) :: skill_types.SkillToolArgs end
    return ({} :: any) :: skill_types.SkillToolArgs
end

local function fmt_manifest(files: { skill_types.SkillFile }?): string
    if not files or #files == 0 then return "No files in this skill." end
    local lines: { string } = { "# Files (" .. tostring(#files) .. ")\n" }
    for _, f in ipairs(files) do
        local size = f.size_bytes and (" — " .. tostring(f.size_bytes) .. " bytes") or ""
        lines[#lines + 1] = "- `" .. tostring(f.path) .. "` (" .. tostring(f.kind) .. ")" .. size
    end
    return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

local function fmt_file(file: skill_types.SkillFileContent?): (any, error?)
    if type(file) ~= "table" then return nil, errors.new({ message = "File not found", kind = errors.NOT_FOUND }) end
    local header = "# " .. tostring(file.path) .. " (" .. tostring(file.mime_type or "") .. ")\n"
    if file.encoding == "base64" then
        return header .. "\n[base64]\n" .. tostring(file.content)
    end
    return header .. "\n" .. tostring(file.content)
end

local function handler(args: any): (any, error?)
    local parsed_args = tool_args(args)
    local action = tostring(parsed_args.action)

    if action == "list" then
        local files, err = funcs.call(SKILL_LIST_FILES, {
            skill_id = parsed_args.skill_id, version = parsed_args.version, kind = parsed_args.kind,
        })
        if err then return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring(err), kind = errors.INTERNAL }) end
        return fmt_manifest(files :: { skill_types.SkillFile }?)
    end

    if action == "read" then
        local file, err = funcs.call(SKILL_READ_FILE, {
            skill_id = parsed_args.skill_id,
            path = parsed_args.path,
            version = parsed_args.version,
            max_bytes = parsed_args.max_bytes,
            format = parsed_args.format,
        })
        if err then return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring(err), kind = errors.INTERNAL }) end
        return fmt_file(file :: skill_types.SkillFileContent?)
    end

    return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring("unknown action '" .. action .. "'. Available: list, read"), kind = errors.INVALID })
end

-- Skill tool — the agent-facing surface over the skill store.
--
-- Progressive disclosure: the agent calls `list` to see skill names + descriptions
-- (cheap), `use` to load a skill's full body only when it needs it, and `save`/
-- `refine` to author or improve a skill from what it just did (the self-improving
-- loop). `agent_id` scopes a skill to a specific agent — that's how one agent
-- manages skills for another (access-checked in the store). Returns markdown.

local funcs = require("funcs")
local ctx = require("ctx")
local active_set = require("active_set")
local skill_types = require("types")

local SKILL_GET = "kickside.skills:skill_get"

-- Maps each tool action to the store method that backs it. Keep in sync with the
-- action enum in the tool's input_schema (_index.yaml). activate/deactivate are
-- handled separately below: they mutate the session's active set, not the store.
local ACTION_FN = {
    list = "skill_list",
    use = "skill_get",
    save = "skill_create",
    refine = "skill_refine",
    delete = "skill_delete",
    share = "skill_share",
    unshare = "skill_share",
}

local function tool_args(args: any): skill_types.SkillToolArgs
    if type(args) == "table" then return (args :: any) :: skill_types.SkillToolArgs end
    return ({} :: any) :: skill_types.SkillToolArgs
end

local function fmt_list(rows: { skill_types.SkillSummary }?): string
    if not rows or #rows == 0 then return "No skills found." end
    local lines: { string } = { "# Skills (" .. tostring(#rows) .. ")\n" }
    for i, s in ipairs(rows) do
        lines[#lines + 1] = tostring(i) .. ". **" .. tostring(s.name or "(untitled)") .. "**  `" .. tostring(s.skill_id or "") .. "`"
        if s.description then lines[#lines + 1] = "   - " .. tostring(s.description) end
        if s.agent_id then lines[#lines + 1] = "   - agent: " .. tostring(s.agent_id) end
    end
    return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

-- Render a skill for `use`: its body plus a compact FILE MANIFEST (paths + kind,
-- not contents). The agent reads a file's contents on demand via the SkillFile
-- tool, so loading a skill never pulls every reference/asset into context.
local function fmt_skill(s: skill_types.Skill?, files: { skill_types.SkillFile }?): (any, error?)
    if type(s) ~= "table" then return nil, errors.new({ message = "Skill not found", kind = errors.NOT_FOUND }) end
    local skill = s :: skill_types.Skill
    local header = "# " .. tostring(skill.name or "") .. " (v" .. tostring(skill.version or 1) .. ")\n"
    local desc = skill.description and ("> " .. tostring(skill.description) .. "\n\n") or ""
    local out = header .. desc .. tostring(skill.body or "")

    if files and #files > 0 then
        local lines: { string } = { "\n\n## Files (read on demand with the SkillFile tool)" }
        for _, f in ipairs(files) do
            lines[#lines + 1] = "- `" .. tostring(f.path) .. "` (" .. tostring(f.kind) .. ")"
        end
        out = out .. table.concat(lines, "\n")
    end
    return out
end

-- activate/deactivate maintain the session's active skill set (active_skills in
-- the session context). The active_skills prompt func injects those bodies into
-- the prompt each step, so activation keeps a skill loaded across turns until the
-- agent deactivates it — distinct from `use`, a one-shot read. The new set is
-- returned as a control directive the session persists; we read the current set
-- back through ctx (the session context is merged into the tool's exec context).
local function handle_active(action: string, args: skill_types.SkillToolArgs): (any, error?)
    local skill_id = args.skill_id
    if type(skill_id) ~= "string" or (skill_id :: string) == "" then
        return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring("skill_id is required to " .. action .. " a skill."), kind = errors.INVALID })
    end
    local current = active_set.parse(ctx.get("active_skills"))

    if action == "activate" then
        if active_set.has(current, skill_id) then
            return { message = "Skill `" .. skill_id .. "` is already active." }
        end
        -- Confirm the actor can read the skill before activating it; a skill that
        -- cannot be loaded must not enter the active set.
        local skill, err = funcs.call(SKILL_GET, { skill_id = skill_id })
        if err then return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring(err), kind = errors.INTERNAL }) end
        local s = skill :: skill_types.Skill
        return {
            message = "Activated **" .. tostring(s.name or skill_id) .. "** `" .. skill_id ..
                "`. It is now in your prompt under \"Active skills\" — follow it directly; " ..
                "deactivate it when you are done.",
            _control = { context = { session = { set = { active_skills = active_set.add(current, skill_id) } } } },
        }
    end

    -- deactivate
    if not active_set.has(current, skill_id) then
        return { message = "Skill `" .. skill_id .. "` is not active." }
    end
    return {
        message = "Deactivated skill `" .. skill_id .. "`. It is no longer in your prompt.",
        _control = { context = { session = { set = { active_skills = active_set.remove(current, skill_id) } } } },
    }
end

local function handler(args: any): (any, error?)
    local parsed_args = tool_args(args)
    local action = tostring(parsed_args.action)

    if action == "activate" or action == "deactivate" then
        return handle_active(action, parsed_args)
    end

    local fn = ACTION_FN[action]
    if not fn then
        return nil, errors.new({ message = "unknown action '" .. action .. "'. Available: " ..
            "list, use, activate, deactivate, save, refine, delete, share, unshare", kind = errors.INVALID })
    end

    -- unshare is share with revoke semantics; carry that through to the store.
    if action == "unshare" then parsed_args.action = "revoke" end

    local result, err = funcs.call("kickside.skills:" .. fn, parsed_args)
    if err then return nil, errors.new({ message = tostring(err), kind = errors.INTERNAL }) end

    if action == "list" then return fmt_list(result :: { skill_types.SkillSummary }) end
    if action == "use" then
        -- Load the file manifest alongside the body; a manifest failure (e.g. an
        -- old skill with no files) still renders the body.
        local files = funcs.call("kickside.skills:skill_list_files", { skill_id = parsed_args.skill_id })
        return fmt_skill(result :: skill_types.Skill, files :: { skill_types.SkillFile }?)
    end
    if action == "save" then return "Saved skill `" .. tostring(result) .. "`." end
    if action == "refine" then
        local r = result :: skill_types.RefineResult?
        if r and r.version then
            return "Refined skill `" .. tostring(r.skill_id) .. "` to version " .. tostring(r.version) .. "."
        end
        return "Updated skill `" .. tostring(r and r.skill_id) .. "`."
    end
    if action == "delete" then
        local r = result :: skill_types.DeleteResult?
        return "Deleted skill `" .. tostring(r and r.skill_id) .. "`."
    end
    if action == "share" or action == "unshare" then
        local r = result :: skill_types.ShareResult?
        local verb = action == "unshare" and "Unshared" or "Shared"
        return verb .. " skill `" .. tostring(r and r.skill_id) .. "` with " .. tostring(r and r.user_id) .. "."
    end
    return "ok"
end

return { handler = handler }

# kickside/skills

Reusable agent procedures ("skills") for Kickside.

A skill is a component (identity / access / sharing / discovery) whose thread is
its append-only version history. A registered projection folds that history into
the current read-model body. Bundle files are upload artifacts referenced by the
version event, so the module does not own a parallel skill database schema.

This module owns:

- The skill store (`kickside.skills:skill_create` / `skill_get` / `skill_list` /
  `skill_list_files` / `skill_read_file` / `skill_refine` / `skill_delete` /
  `skill_share`) — per-method dispatchers over the thread-backed state reader and
  writer, each running under the caller's actor so the component service enforces
  access.
- The bundle helpers (`bundle/frontmatter.lua` — a bounded SKILL.md frontmatter
  parser, and `bundle/normalize.lua` — the SkillBundle normalizer).
- The HTTP API: `GET /skills`, `GET /skills/{id}`,
  `GET /skills/{id}/versions`, `POST /skills`, `PATCH /skills/{id}`,
  and `DELETE /skills/{id}`. Sharing is exposed through the Skill tool and the
  `skill_share` store function, not as an HTTP route.
- The `skill_runtime` contract (activate / list_files / read_file).
- The **Skills** agent trait (`kickside.skills.traits:skills`): a dual-mode trait
  whose static prompt + `Skill` tool give on-demand discovery, load, author, and
  refine of any readable skill (`use` returns the body + a compact file manifest);
  a `SkillFile` tool reads bundled files on demand; and a build func
  (`init_skills`) pins specific skills' bodies + manifests into an agent's prompt
  when the agent supplies `context.skill_ids`.

## Script execution (follow-on, self-contained)

Bundled `scripts/` files are **stored, not executed** in V1. The architecture spot
is reserved entirely inside this module so a follow-on runner can be added without
touching any other package:

- `skill_files.kind = "script"` + the `executable` flag are persisted; a script's
  language is inferred from its extension into the file metadata.
- A version's `allowed_tools_json` / `compatibility_json` are persisted.
- `kickside.skills:skill_runtime` exposes only implemented file-runtime methods:
  `activate`, `list_files`, and `read_file`.
- `runtime/` is the home for a future runner: a `docker_runner.lua` (a finite job over
  `userspace.docker:containers`, resolved against the `kickside.skill_runner`
  registry allowlist — not arbitrary images) + a `stage_bundle.lua` (stage a
  version's scripts/assets to a temp dir, mount `/skill` read-only + `/out`
  read-write). A future `SkillScript` tool slots into the trait's tool list
  alongside `Skill` + `SkillFile`.

## Boundary

skills is permission-agnostic. The host router enforces auth + endpoint firewall;
per-skill access is the component service's job (`component.validate_access`).

skills depends on `kickside/component`, `kickside/contract`, `kickside/core`, and
`kickside/uploads`. It registers the `agent.trait` + `tool`
registry entries the agents module discovers through the registry — there is no
code coupling to the agents module.

## Dependency interface

The consuming host wires these via `ns.dependency`:

- `api_router` — required router the six HTTP routes attach to; must
  enforce auth + endpoint firewall.
- `ui_server` — required HTTP server for the bundled Skills UI.
- `upload_storage` — required filesystem for bundle upload artifacts.

## Test

```
make test
```

Boots the Skills dependency graph and runs the co-located `*_test.lua` suites
(store CRUD/share, the Skill tool e2e, and skill pinning into a compiled agent).

local component = require("component")
local types = require("types")

-- Skills version-history projection worker. The runner invokes it (worker_input_mode
-- = prefetch_events) with a batch of new skill events + the projection's current
-- body; it folds each created/updated event into body.versions and advances
-- current_version, returning the body + last_seq. The body IS the read model
-- (kickside_projection): reader.lua serves get/list_versions/list_files/read_file
-- from it without replaying events, so the history survives event retention.
-- body.meta carries the engine's worker config and must be preserved untouched.
local M = {}

local function trim(value: any): string
    if type(value) ~= "string" then return "" end
    return (value:gsub("^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1"))
end

local function as_table(value: any): any
    if type(value) == "table" then return value end
    return {}
end

local function head_version(body: any): any
    local versions = type(body.versions) == "table" and body.versions or {}
    local current = tonumber(body.current_version) or 0
    local head: any = nil
    for _, v in ipairs(versions :: { any }) do
        local n = tonumber((v :: any).version) or 0
        if current > 0 and n == current then return v end
        if not head or n > (tonumber((head :: any).version) or 0) then head = v end
    end
    return head or {}
end

local function sync_public_meta(input: any, body: any): (boolean, string?)
    local skill_id = trim(body.skill_id)
    if skill_id == "" then return true, nil end

    local versions = type(body.versions) == "table" and body.versions or {}
    local head = head_version(body)
    local component_api = (type(input.component) == "table" and input.component) or component

    local ok, err = component_api.set_meta(skill_id, {
        version = tonumber(body.current_version) or tonumber((head :: any).version) or 0,
        version_count = #versions,
        file_count = tonumber((head :: any).file_count) or 0,
        bundle_size = tonumber((head :: any).bundle_size) or 0,
        last_version_at = (head :: any).created_at,
    })
    if ok == true then return true, nil end
    return false, tostring(err or "component.set_meta failed")
end

-- Upsert a version record into body.versions (replace same version, else append).
local function put_version(body: any, record: any)
    local versions = type(body.versions) == "table" and body.versions or {}
    local ver = tonumber(record.version) or 0
    local replaced = false
    for i, v in ipairs(versions :: { any }) do
        if (tonumber(v.version) or 0) == ver then
            versions[i] = record
            replaced = true
            break
        end
    end
    if not replaced then versions[#versions + 1] = record end
    body.versions = versions
    if ver > (tonumber(body.current_version) or 0) then body.current_version = ver end
end

-- Fold one event into the body.
local function apply(body: any, event: any)
    local etype = trim((event :: any).type)
    if etype ~= types.EVENT.CREATED and etype ~= types.EVENT.UPDATED then return end
    local ebody = as_table((event :: any).body)
    local skill_id = trim(ebody.skill_id)
    if skill_id ~= "" then body.skill_id = skill_id end
    local record = {
        version = tonumber(ebody.version) or ((tonumber(body.current_version) or 0) + 1),
        body = type(ebody.body) == "string" and ebody.body or "",
        name = ebody.name,
        description = ebody.description,
        license = ebody.license,
        allowed_tools = type(ebody.allowed_tools) == "table" and ebody.allowed_tools or nil,
        compatibility = type(ebody.compatibility) == "table" and ebody.compatibility or nil,
        metadata = type(ebody.metadata) == "table" and ebody.metadata or nil,
        source = type(ebody.source) == "table" and ebody.source or nil,
        files = type(ebody.files) == "table" and ebody.files or {},
        file_count = tonumber(ebody.file_count) or 0,
        bundle_size = tonumber(ebody.bundle_size) or 0,
        created_at = (event :: any).created_at,
    }
    put_version(body, record)
end

-- run(input): the worker entrypoint. input.projection.body is the carried read
-- model; input.events is the new batch; input.range.to_seq is the new head.
function M.run(input: any): any
    input = type(input) == "table" and input or {}
    local projection = type(input.projection) == "table" and input.projection or {}
    local body: any = type(projection.body) == "table" and projection.body or {}
    if body.versions == nil then body.versions = {} end
    if body.current_version == nil then body.current_version = 0 end

    local events = type(input.events) == "table" and input.events or {}
    for _, e in ipairs(events :: { any }) do apply(body, e) end

    local meta_ok, meta_err = sync_public_meta(input, body)
    if not meta_ok then return nil, meta_err end

    local range = type(input.range) == "table" and input.range or {}
    return { body = body, last_seq = tonumber(range.to_seq) or nil }
end

return M

-- Coordinates the two durable writes made by a skill refinement: public component
-- metadata and the skill's immutable version event. These stores are owned behind
-- separate contracts and expose no shared transaction, so a database transaction
-- here would be fake atomicity.
--
-- Metadata is written first because component.set_meta has a deterministic inverse;
-- an appended thread event does not. The append boundary accepts an exact replay of
-- its durable version key and rejects a same-key/different-body collision.

local M = {}
local errors = require("errors")

type Collaborators = {
    get_meta: any,
    set_meta: any,
    append: any,
}

local function restoration(current_meta: any, desired: any): (any, { string })
    local fields: { [string]: any } = {}
    local delete_keys: { string } = {}
    current_meta = type(current_meta) == "table" and current_meta or {}

    for key, _ in pairs(desired :: { [string]: any }) do
        local previous = (current_meta :: { [string]: any })[key]
        if previous == nil then
            table.insert(delete_keys, key)
        else
            fields[key] = previous
        end
    end
    table.sort(delete_keys)
    return fields, delete_keys
end

function M.apply(skill_id: string, desired: any, collaborators: Collaborators): (boolean, any?)
    -- Snapshot before either durable write. Besides making rollback exact, this
    -- proves the component still exists and is readable before the event is tried.
    local current_meta, snapshot_err = collaborators.get_meta(skill_id)
    if snapshot_err or type(current_meta) ~= "table" then
        return false, "component metadata preflight failed: "
            .. tostring(snapshot_err or "invalid metadata snapshot")
    end
    local restore_fields, delete_keys = restoration(current_meta, desired)

    local meta_ok, meta_err = collaborators.set_meta(skill_id, desired)
    if meta_ok ~= true then
        return false, "component metadata update failed: " .. tostring(meta_err or "unknown error")
    end

    local append_err = collaborators.append()
    if not append_err then return true, nil end

    local rollback_ok, rollback_err = collaborators.set_meta(skill_id, restore_fields, {
        delete_keys = delete_keys,
    })
    if rollback_ok ~= true then
        local message = "append updated failed: " .. tostring(append_err)
            .. "; component metadata rollback failed: " .. tostring(rollback_err or "unknown error")
        if type(append_err) == "userdata" then
            return false, errors.new({ message = message, kind = append_err:kind(),
                retryable = append_err:retryable() })
        end
        return false, message
    end
    if type(append_err) == "userdata" then return false, append_err end
    return false, "append updated failed: " .. tostring(append_err)
        .. "; component metadata rolled back"
end

return M

-- Write side of the skills slice (commands). A skill is a component (identity /
-- access / kind, via the component contract) whose primary kickside.core thread
-- events ARE the version history; a registered projection folds them into the
-- read-model body the reader serves. Bundled files are upload artifacts under one
-- bundle upload per skill (upload_id = skill_id), referenced by artifact_id in each
-- version's event manifest. create registers the component, ensures the thread +
-- projection + bundle upload, stores the first version's files as artifacts, and
-- appends the `created` event; refine appends an `updated` event (files replaced or
-- carried forward by artifact_id) and patches the public meta; delete removes the
-- component (its deletable tears down the thread + bundle); share grants/revokes
-- access. Access is gated through the component contract; reads live in the reader.

local component = require("component")
local uuid = require("uuid")
local hash = require("hash")
local base64 = require("base64")
local security = require("security")
local contract = require("contract")
local errors = require("errors")
local skill_types = require("types")
local normalize = require("normalize")
local state = require("skill_state")
local artifact_content_repo = require("artifact_content_repo")
local upload_record_repo = require("upload_record_repo")
local upload_query_repo = require("upload_query_repo")
local skill_storage = require("skill_storage")
local refine_consistency = require("refine_consistency")
local version_append = require("version_append")

local M = {}

local is_str = normalize.is_str

local function over_limit(field: string, value: any, max: integer): string?
    if type(value) == "string" and #(value :: string) > max then
        return field .. " too long (max " .. tostring(max) .. ")"
    end
    return nil
end

local function valid_status(status: any): boolean
    return status == skill_types.STATUS.ACTIVE or status == skill_types.STATUS.ARCHIVED
end

local function actor_id(): string
    local actor = security.actor()
    if not actor then return "" end
    local id = actor:id()
    return id and tostring(id) or ""
end

-- The one canonical threads seam: the kickside.core:threads contract, opened under
-- the ambient caller identity, never a private *_method function-id.
local THREADS_CONTRACT = "kickside.core:threads"

local function threads(): (any?, string?)
    local def, gerr = contract.get(THREADS_CONTRACT)
    if gerr or not def then return nil, "threads contract unavailable: " .. tostring(gerr) end
    local inst, oerr = (def :: any):open()
    if oerr or not inst then return nil, "threads open failed: " .. tostring(oerr) end
    return inst, nil
end

-- Resolve a fetched file's raw bytes from its content + encoding. Text is stored
-- as-is; base64 is decoded so the artifact holds real bytes.
local function decode_content(file: skill_types.SkillFileInput): (string?, string?)
    local content = file.content
    if content == nil then return "" end
    if type(content) ~= "string" then return nil, "file content must be a string" end
    if file.encoding == skill_types.ENCODING.BASE64 then
        local bytes, derr = base64.decode(content :: string)
        if derr then return nil, "base64 decode failed: " .. tostring(derr) end
        return bytes
    end
    return content :: string
end

type PreparedFile = {
    path: string,
    kind: string,
    mime_type: string?,
    content: string,
    size_bytes: integer,
    sha256: string,
    executable: boolean,
    metadata: skill_types.Map?,
}

-- Validate + normalize the incoming file list into prepared files (raw bytes +
-- descriptors). Returns (files, total_bytes, err).
local function prepare_files(files: any): ({ PreparedFile }?, integer, string?)
    if files == nil then return {}, 0 end
    if type(files) ~= "table" then return nil, 0, "files must be an array" end
    local list = files :: { skill_types.SkillFileInput }
    if #list > skill_types.LIMITS.FILE_COUNT then
        return nil, 0, "too many files (max " .. tostring(skill_types.LIMITS.FILE_COUNT) .. ")"
    end

    local out: { PreparedFile } = {}
    local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
    local total = 0
    for _, raw in ipairs(list) do
        local nf = normalize.normalize_file(raw)
        local path, perr = normalize.clean_path(nf.path)
        if perr then return nil, 0, perr end
        if seen[path :: string] then return nil, 0, "duplicate file path: " .. (path :: string) end
        seen[path :: string] = true

        local bytes, berr = decode_content(raw)
        if berr then return nil, 0, berr end
        local b = bytes :: string
        if #b > skill_types.LIMITS.FILE then
            return nil, 0, "file too large: " .. (path :: string) .. " (max " .. tostring(skill_types.LIMITS.FILE) .. ")"
        end
        total = total + #b
        if total > skill_types.LIMITS.BUNDLE then
            return nil, 0, "bundle too large (max " .. tostring(skill_types.LIMITS.BUNDLE) .. ")"
        end

        out[#out + 1] = {
            path = path :: string,
            kind = nf.kind,
            mime_type = nf.mime_type,
            content = b,
            size_bytes = #b,
            sha256 = hash.sha256(b),
            executable = nf.executable == true,
            metadata = type(nf.metadata) == "table" and nf.metadata or nil,
        }
    end
    return out, total :: integer
end

-- Ensure the skill's bundle upload exists (the container artifacts hang off). One
-- per skill, upload_id = skill_id. Idempotent: a present row is fine.
local function ensure_bundle_upload(skill_id: string, total: integer): string?
    local existing = upload_query_repo.get(skill_id)
    if existing then return nil end
    local _, err = upload_record_repo.create(
        skill_id, actor_id(), math.max(1, total), "application/x-skill-bundle",
        skill_storage.id(), "skill-bundle/" .. skill_id, "skill_bundle",
        { skill_id = skill_id }, "completed"
    )
    -- A concurrent create races to the same uuid; typed conflict is idempotent.
    if err and not errors.is(err, errors.CONFLICT) then
        return "bundle upload: " .. tostring(err)
    end
    return nil
end

-- Store prepared files as artifacts under the skill's bundle upload; build the
-- version manifest (descriptors + artifact_id). Returns (manifest, total, err).
local function store_files(skill_id: string, files: { PreparedFile }): ({ skill_types.SkillFileManifest }?, integer, string?)
    local manifest: { skill_types.SkillFileManifest } = {}
    local total = 0
    for _, f in ipairs(files) do
        local artifact, aerr = artifact_content_repo.create_artifact({
            upload_id = skill_id,
            kind = f.kind,
            mime_type = f.mime_type or "application/octet-stream",
            content = f.content,
            label = f.path,
            checksum = f.sha256,
            metadata = { path = f.path, executable = f.executable, skill_metadata = f.metadata },
        })
        if aerr or not artifact then return nil, 0, "store file " .. f.path .. ": " .. tostring(aerr) end
        total = total + f.size_bytes
        manifest[#manifest + 1] = {
            path = f.path,
            kind = f.kind,
            mime_type = f.mime_type,
            size_bytes = f.size_bytes,
            sha256 = f.sha256,
            executable = f.executable,
            metadata = f.metadata,
            artifact_id = tostring((artifact :: any).artifact_id),
        }
    end
    return manifest, total :: integer
end

local function bundle_total(manifest: { skill_types.SkillFileManifest }): integer
    local total = 0
    for _, m in ipairs(manifest) do total = total + (tonumber(m.size_bytes) or 0) end
    return total :: integer
end

-- Append a version event to the skill's history thread, then advance the
-- kind's history projection through it (the threads read-after-write seam), so
-- the version is readable when the write returns: an agent saves a skill and
-- activates it in consecutive calls.
local function append_version(thread_id: string, etype: string, record: skill_types.Map): any?
    -- thread_id == skill_id (the component's primary thread). emit ensures it + the
    -- kind's declared history projection on first append.
    local inst, terr = threads()
    if terr then return terr end
    local append_err = version_append.append(
        inst,
        thread_id,
        etype,
        record,
        skill_types.SKILL_IMPL,
        skill_types.THREAD_CLASS
    )
    if append_err then return append_err end
    local _, catch_up_err = (inst :: any):catch_up_projection({ thread_id = thread_id, kind = skill_types.PROJECTION_KIND })
    if catch_up_err then return catch_up_err end
    return nil
end

local function latest_version(thread_id: string): (any?, string?)
    local inst, terr = threads()
    if terr or not inst then return nil, terr end
    return version_append.latest(inst, thread_id, skill_types.EVENT.CREATED, skill_types.EVENT.UPDATED)
end

-- The frontmatter fields a version event carries.
type Frontmatter = {
    license: any,
    allowed_tools: any,
    compatibility: any,
    metadata: any,
    source: any,
}

local function frontmatter(args: skill_types.Map): Frontmatter
    return {
        license = is_str(args.license) and args.license or nil,
        allowed_tools = type(args.allowed_tools) == "table" and args.allowed_tools or nil,
        compatibility = type(args.compatibility) == "table" and args.compatibility or nil,
        metadata = type(args.metadata) == "table" and args.metadata or nil,
        source = type(args.source) == "table" and args.source or nil,
    }
end

-- create: register the skill component, ensure its history thread + projection +
-- bundle upload, store the first version's files as artifacts, and append the
-- `created` event. Returns the skill_id.
function M.create(args: any): (string?, any?)
    args = args or {}
    local create_args = args :: skill_types.SkillCreateArgs
    if not is_str(create_args.name) then return nil, "name is required" end
    if not is_str(create_args.description) then return nil, "description is required (drives skill discovery)" end
    local lim_err = over_limit("name", create_args.name, skill_types.LIMITS.NAME)
        or over_limit("description", create_args.description, skill_types.LIMITS.DESCRIPTION)
        or over_limit("body", create_args.body, skill_types.LIMITS.BODY)
    if lim_err then return nil, lim_err end
    if is_str(create_args.status) and not valid_status(create_args.status) then
        return nil, "status must be 'active' or 'archived'"
    end

    -- A skill can target a specific agent (scoped to it) or be user-global. Creating
    -- one FOR an agent requires write access to that agent.
    if is_str(create_args.agent_id) then
        local _, aerr = component.validate_access(create_args.agent_id :: string, component.ACCESS.WRITE)
        if aerr then return nil, "write access to the target agent is required" end
    end

    local svc, serr = component.get_service()
    if serr or not svc then return nil, "component service unavailable: " .. tostring(serr) end

    local skill_id = uuid.v4()

    local meta: skill_types.Map = {
        title = create_args.name,
        comment = create_args.description,
        class = skill_types.SKILL_CLASS,
        status = is_str(create_args.status) and create_args.status or skill_types.STATUS.ACTIVE,
    }
    if is_str(create_args.agent_id) then meta.agent_id = create_args.agent_id end
    if is_str(create_args.icon) then meta.icon = create_args.icon end

    local reg, rerr = svc:register({ component_id = skill_id, impl_id = skill_types.SKILL_IMPL, meta = meta })
    if rerr or not (reg and reg.success) then
        return nil, "register_component: " .. tostring(rerr or (reg and reg.error) or "unknown")
    end

    local function rollback(e: any): (string?, any?)
        svc:delete({ component_id = skill_id })
        return nil, e
    end

    -- The primary thread is materialized by the core emit path, which applies the
    -- skill kind's declared history projection on first append.
    local thread_id, terr = state.thread_for(skill_id)
    if terr or not thread_id then return rollback("thread: " .. tostring(terr)) end

    local prepared, total, ferr = prepare_files(create_args.files)
    if ferr or not prepared then return rollback(ferr or "file prepare failed") end
    local berr = ensure_bundle_upload(skill_id, total)
    if berr then return rollback(berr) end
    local manifest, mtotal, serr2 = store_files(skill_id, prepared)
    if serr2 or not manifest then return rollback(serr2 or "file store failed") end

    local fm = frontmatter(create_args :: skill_types.Map)
    local record: skill_types.Map = {
        skill_id = skill_id,
        version = 1,
        body = type(create_args.body) == "string" and create_args.body or "",
        name = create_args.name,
        description = create_args.description,
        license = fm.license,
        allowed_tools = fm.allowed_tools,
        compatibility = fm.compatibility,
        metadata = fm.metadata,
        source = fm.source,
        files = manifest,
        file_count = #manifest,
        bundle_size = mtotal,
    }
    local aerr = append_version(thread_id, skill_types.EVENT.CREATED, record)
    if aerr then return rollback(aerr) end
    return skill_id
end

-- refine: append a new version (body + files) and/or patch the public meta. WRITE
-- access required. A new version is cut when body or files change; files default to
-- the prior version's manifest (carried by artifact_id) unless `files` is given,
-- which fully replaces them. Frontmatter carries forward unless replaced. Returns
-- { skill_id, version } (version set iff a new version was written).
function M.refine(args: any): (skill_types.RefineResult?, any?)
    args = args or {}
    local refine_args = args :: skill_types.SkillRefineArgs
    if not is_str(refine_args.skill_id) then return nil, "skill_id is required" end
    local skill_id = refine_args.skill_id :: string
    local has_files = refine_args.files ~= nil
    if not is_str(refine_args.body) and not is_str(refine_args.description) and not is_str(refine_args.status)
        and not is_str(refine_args.icon) and not has_files then
        return nil, "nothing to refine (provide body, description, status, icon, or files)"
    end
    local lim_err = over_limit("body", refine_args.body, skill_types.LIMITS.BODY)
        or over_limit("description", refine_args.description, skill_types.LIMITS.DESCRIPTION)
    if lim_err then return nil, lim_err end
    if is_str(refine_args.status) and not valid_status(refine_args.status) then
        return nil, "status must be 'active' or 'archived'"
    end

    local _, aerr = component.validate_access(skill_id, component.ACCESS.WRITE)
    if aerr then return nil, "write access denied" end

    local meta_fields: skill_types.Map = {}
    if is_str(refine_args.description) then
        meta_fields.comment = refine_args.description
    end
    if is_str(refine_args.status) then
        meta_fields.status = refine_args.status
    end
    if is_str(refine_args.icon) then
        meta_fields.icon = refine_args.icon
    end

    local new_version: integer? = nil
    local append_pending: any = nil
    if is_str(refine_args.body) or has_files then
        local thread_id, terr = state.thread_for(skill_id)
        if terr or not thread_id then return nil, terr or "skill history unavailable" end
        local head, herr = latest_version(thread_id)
        if not head then return nil, herr or "skill not found" end
        new_version = ((tonumber((head :: any).version) or 1) + 1) :: integer

        local body_md = is_str(refine_args.body) and refine_args.body or tostring((head :: any).body or "")
        local fm = frontmatter(refine_args :: skill_types.Map)
        local manifest: { skill_types.SkillFileManifest }
        local mtotal: integer
        if has_files then
            local prepared, total, ferr = prepare_files(refine_args.files)
            if ferr or not prepared then return nil, ferr end
            local bupErr = ensure_bundle_upload(skill_id, total)
            if bupErr then return nil, bupErr end
            local stored, st, serr2 = store_files(skill_id, prepared)
            if serr2 or not stored then return nil, serr2 end
            manifest = stored
            mtotal = st
        else
            -- Carry the head's manifest forward (same artifacts, no re-upload).
            manifest = (type((head :: any).files) == "table" and (head :: any).files or {}) :: { skill_types.SkillFileManifest }
            mtotal = bundle_total(manifest)
        end

        local record: skill_types.Map = {
            skill_id = skill_id,
            version = new_version,
            body = body_md,
            name = is_str(refine_args.name) and refine_args.name or (head :: any).name,
            description = is_str(refine_args.description) and refine_args.description or (head :: any).description,
            license = fm.license ~= nil and fm.license or (head :: any).license,
            allowed_tools = fm.allowed_tools ~= nil and fm.allowed_tools or (head :: any).allowed_tools,
            compatibility = fm.compatibility ~= nil and fm.compatibility or (head :: any).compatibility,
            metadata = fm.metadata ~= nil and fm.metadata or (head :: any).metadata,
            source = fm.source ~= nil and fm.source or (head :: any).source,
            files = manifest,
            file_count = #manifest,
            bundle_size = mtotal,
        }
        append_pending = function(): any?
            return append_version(thread_id, skill_types.EVENT.UPDATED, record)
        end
    end

    local has_meta = next(meta_fields) ~= nil
    if append_pending and has_meta then
        -- Component metadata and the thread event are owned behind separate
        -- contracts. The coordinator snapshots metadata, writes the reversible
        -- side first, and restores it if the append fails or detects a concurrent
        -- same-version writer.
        local svc, svc_err = component.get_service()
        if svc_err or not svc then
            return nil, "component service unavailable: " .. tostring(svc_err)
        end
        local ok, consistency_err = refine_consistency.apply(skill_id, meta_fields, {
            get_meta = function(component_id: string): (any?, string?)
                local result, get_err = svc:get({ component_id = component_id })
                if get_err or not result or result.success == false then
                    return nil, tostring(get_err or (result and result.error) or "not found")
                end
                return type(result.meta) == "table" and result.meta or {}, nil
            end,
            set_meta = component.set_meta,
            append = append_pending,
        })
        if not ok then return nil, consistency_err end
    elseif append_pending then
        local apperr = append_pending()
        if apperr then return nil, apperr end
    elseif has_meta then
        local ok, err = component.set_meta(skill_id, meta_fields)
        if not ok then return nil, "meta update failed: " .. tostring(err) end
    end

    return ({ skill_id = skill_id, version = new_version }) :: skill_types.RefineResult
end

-- share: grant or revoke another user's access to a skill (same component-access
-- model as sharing an agent). ADMIN access required.
function M.share(args: any): (skill_types.ShareResult?, string?)
    args = args or {}
    local share_args = args :: skill_types.SkillShareArgs
    if not is_str(share_args.skill_id) then return nil, "skill_id is required" end
    if not is_str(share_args.user_id) then return nil, "user_id is required" end

    local _, aerr = component.validate_access(share_args.skill_id :: string, component.ACCESS.ADMIN)
    if aerr then return nil, "admin access required to share" end

    local svc, serr = component.get_service()
    if serr or not svc then return nil, "component service unavailable: " .. tostring(serr) end

    local subject = { subject_id = share_args.user_id, subject_type = "user" }
    local res, e
    if share_args.action == "revoke" then
        res, e = svc:revoke_subtree({ root_component_id = share_args.skill_id, subject = subject })
    else
        local access_policy = require("access_policy")
        local access_mask, mask_err = access_policy.normalize_access_mask(share_args.access_mask, component.ACCESS.READ)
        if mask_err then return nil, mask_err end
        res, e = svc:grant_subtree({ root_component_id = share_args.skill_id, subject = subject, access_mask = access_mask })
    end
    if e or not (res and res.success) then
        return nil, "share failed: " .. tostring(e or (res and res.error))
    end
    return ({ skill_id = share_args.skill_id, user_id = share_args.user_id, action = share_args.action or "grant" }) :: skill_types.ShareResult
end

-- delete: remove the skill component. DELETE access required. The component's
-- deletable impl tears down the history thread + the bundle upload (artifacts).
function M.delete(args: any): (skill_types.DeleteResult?, string?)
    args = args or {}
    local delete_args = args :: skill_types.SkillDeleteArgs
    if not is_str(delete_args.skill_id) then return nil, "skill_id is required" end

    local _, aerr = component.validate_access(delete_args.skill_id :: string, component.ACCESS.DELETE)
    if aerr then return nil, "delete access denied" end

    local svc, serr = component.get_service()
    if serr or not svc then return nil, "component service unavailable: " .. tostring(serr) end
    local res, e = svc:delete({ component_id = delete_args.skill_id })
    if e or not (res and res.success) then
        return nil, "delete_component: " .. tostring(e or (res and res.error))
    end
    return ({ skill_id = delete_args.skill_id }) :: skill_types.DeleteResult
end

return M
